A method that never reads `this` does not need an instance. Callers still have to create one to reach it. Make it `static`, or move it out of the class.

Methods, getters, setters, and functions stored in instance fields are checked. Constructors, static members, and abstract members are not.

It is the TypeScript version of `class-methods-use-this` and reports the same code. Turn on one of the two, not both.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
class Invoice {
  total = 0;

  format(amount: number) {
    return amount.toFixed(2);
  }

  round = (amount: number) => Math.round(amount);
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
class Invoice {
  total = 0;

  static format(amount: number) {
    return amount.toFixed(2);
  }

  print() {
    return Invoice.format(this.total);
  }
}
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exceptMethods` | `[]` | Names of methods to skip. Write a private method as `"#name"`. |
| `enforceForClassFields` | `true` | Also check functions stored in instance fields, such as `round` above. |
| `ignoreOverrideMethods` | `false` | Skip members marked `override`. |
| `ignoreClassesThatImplementAnInterface` | `false` | `true` skips every member of a class that has an `implements` clause. `"public-fields"` still checks its `private` and `protected` members. |

A subclass has to keep the shape of the method it overrides, so it cannot make it `static`:

{/* good {"options": [{"ignoreOverrideMethods": true}]} */}
```ts
class Widget {
  name = "widget";
  render() {
    return this.name;
  }
}

class Spinner extends Widget {
  override render() {
    return "...";
  }
}
```

The same holds for a method that an interface asks for. With `"public-fields"`, `render` is skipped and `frame` is reported. With `true`, neither is reported.

{/* bad {"options": [{"ignoreClassesThatImplementAnInterface": "public-fields"}], "count": 1} */}
```ts
interface Renderable {
  render(): string;
}

class Spinner implements Renderable {
  render() {
    return "...";
  }
  private frame() {
    return 0;
  }
}
```
